title: Where to eat in Lisbon: 15 restaurants, tascas and pastry shops
desc: Lisbon restaurants, tavernas, sandwich counters and pastry shops, split into sit-down meals and quick bites, sweets & drinks.

items.title: Parra Wine Bistro
items.memo: Campo de Ourique wine bistro; go for the Alentejo black pork. Around EUR 50+ each.

items.title: Faz Frio
items.memo: Principe Real classic; save room for the chocolate mousse.

items.title: Taberna Sal Grosso
items.memo: Small Alfama taberna; the cod a Bras is the dish to order.

items.title: A Merendinha do Arco Bandeira
items.memo: Baixa spot for clams in garlic and herb oil, about EUR 15-25.

items.title: Uma Marisqueira
items.memo: Known for one thing: arroz de marisco (seafood rice).

items.title: Trobadores
items.memo: Medieval-style tavern; order the flaming chorizo.

items.title: O Segredo D'Alfama
items.memo: Three-course dinner with Fado in Alfama.

items.title: Ourives Petisqueira
items.memo: Petiscos to share, like shrimp and calamari, from about EUR 20.

items.title: Arca Bistro
items.memo: Piri piri chicken served with tzatziki; about EUR 30-50.

items.title: As Bifanas do Afonso
items.memo: Pork bifana sandwich for roughly EUR 3-5.

items.title: Confeitaria Nacional
items.memo: Old Praca da Figueira pastry shop; try the bolo de berlim.

items.title: Manteigaria (Rua Augusta)
items.memo: Pastel de nata on Rua Augusta, EUR 3-5.

items.title: Time Out Market
items.memo: Food hall in Mercado da Ribeira; Iberian ham is the pick.

items.title: A Ginjinha
items.memo: Cherry liqueur shot near Rossio, about EUR 1.50.
